summary: We are testing whether a MaxRects bin-packing algorithm with exhaustive item-ordering search across multiple placement heuristics can score above 90/100 on a 2D rectangular knapsack problem (problem #47) with 8–12 item types, bins up to 2000×2000, optional 90° rotations, and a 1-second time limit per test case.
key_points: Single arm (h-main): Implements MaxRects packer with 3 heuristics (BSSF, BAF, BL), 7 sorting strategies, exhaustive permutation search over item-type orderings (feasible for M≤10, capped at 20K permutations for M>10), plus time-budgeted random shuffling — all within a 0.88s wall-clock budget.

Confirmation criterion: Judge score consistently above 90 (averaged across 15 hidden test cases). Scores below 90 trigger diagnostics — JSON format issues, rotation-flag mishandling, time-limit overruns, or free-rectangle pruning losses.

Key risk factors: (1) Permutation exhaustion may be insufficient for M=11–12 (up to 479M orderings), relying on heuristic orderings and random search to compensate; (2) MaxRects free-rectangle list can grow large on big bins, potentially exceeding the 1s time limit; (3) The scoring formula rewards beating a baseline shelf heuristic relative to a fractional upper bound, so even good packings may score modestly if the upper bound is loose.
